summary: Submitted unchanged; validated as no_change with no effects, so no record is created or duplicated, and the newly registered question @q_stale_snapshot_propagation stands for a continuation. The run's deliverable is complete: two sourced defects in hashicorp/raft's RestoreCommittedLogs path, each with an experiment-cited account whose conclusion is violated and whose defect claim is asserted. Configuration recovery (98ee8dfd5fac4b84915f91ed4b094bcf-question-0) rests on eight retained receipts - the single-voter recovery cases with flag-off controls, the three-voter commit-rule witness reproduced in four receipts, the durable-snapshot corruption that survived a flag-off restart, the authority pair with a repeat in which its premise failed and a revision that enforces it, and the two-voter vote boundary in two executions that limits the claim to candidacy rather than participation. Replay completion (29e4214f5ee146b393957fa23a33a73d-question-0) rests on eleven - the block pair, the measured bound pair, the availability consequence at two batch sizes, the exact 128-delivered-batch boundary at two batch sizes, and default-configuration reachability reproduced twice - with the bound stated as 128 x MaxAppendEntries delivered batches. Three knowledge corrections (tuple-counted batching, randomized snapshot cadence, enumerated configuration writers) are recorded with changed premises, affected uses marked and gaps answered; 54 claims across 14 receipts were verified against the observations with no discrepancy and all cited source anchors re-checked; one internal contradiction was repaired; the predecessor receipt that failed inside its own harness is retained without a comparison claim; and the one direction that could not be exercised in this allocation - whether a stale snapshot's configuration propagates through InstallSnapshot - is registered with its rival readings and a concrete discriminator. Remaining limits are structural and recorded per account, and expiry preserves this state.
